cleanIntro: The Model 9422 is a takedown rifle, and Winchester's book publishes the whole takedown: one screw out, the rifle in two halves, and the bolt slide and breech bolt out of the receiver. That is the field strip, and it is also as far as the book goes — it forbids taking the rifle apart any further. The safety on this rifle is the hammer's half-cock notch, not a button, so every step below starts and ends with the hammer at half-cock. The book covers both versions: the rifle that takes .22 Short, Long and Long Rifle, and the .22 WMR rifle.

steps.title: Hammer to half-cock, then empty the tube out of the muzzle end
steps.action: With the hammer at half-cock and the muzzle pointed up, twist the magazine tube plug to unlock it and draw the inner magazine tube out of the outer tube. Then tip the rifle muzzle-down over a container so the cartridges slide out of the loading port. The tube is spring-loaded, so it moves under your hand rather than sitting still; keep hold of it. The mistake is tipping the rifle before the inner tube is pulled far enough to clear the loading port, which leaves rounds behind it in the outer tube.
steps.prose: A rimfire tube rifle unloads through the front, not the action. Shaking out the tube before you work the lever means the lever only has the chambered round left to eject.
steps.quote: Place the hammer in the safety (half-cock) position. With the rifle pointed upward, withdraw the inside magazine tube from the gun. Tip the gun downward allowing the cartridges to slide out into a suitable container.
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — To Unload the Magazine and Chamber
steps.warn: Muzzle up to pull the tube, muzzle down to pour — never toward anyone.

steps.title: Tube back in, lever down, and look for the coloured follower
steps.action: Push the inner tube back in and lock it, then swing the finger lever fully down to eject whatever is in the chamber. Look into the open action: you should see an empty chamber, no cartridge anywhere in the action, and the coloured magazine follower. Seeing the follower is the proof the tube is empty — a cartridge would sit in front of it. Do not count on the round you expected to fly out; look.
steps.prose: Working the lever also cocks the hammer, so the next step brings it back down to half-cock before anything else happens.
steps.quote: Operate the finger lever, opening the action to eject the round from the chamber. Look into the open action making sure there are no cartridges in the action, and see both the empty chamber and the colored magazine follower.
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — To Unload the Magazine and Chamber
steps.warn: Empty chamber AND the coloured follower in view, or the rifle is not clear.

steps.title: Ease the hammer back down to half-cock under your thumb
steps.action: Hold the hammer spur back firmly with your thumb, press the trigger just enough to release the hammer from full cock, then take your finger straight off the trigger and let the hammer down slowly until it stops in the half-cock notch. You will feel it catch there rather than travel all the way down. A slipped thumb is the classic way a lever gun fires, which is why the rifle is already empty and still pointed somewhere safe. Never force the trigger to drop the hammer out of half-cock: Winchester warns that it strains the parts and weakens the notch that is this rifle's only safety.
steps.prose: The half-cock notch is the 9422's safety position. Winchester also warns it will not necessarily prevent a discharge if the rifle is dropped or jarred, so it is a help, not a substitute for an empty chamber.
steps.quote: Immediately remove your finger from the trigger and slowly and carefully allow the hammer to lower into the “safety” half-cock position (Figure 13).
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions — HOW TO PLACE THE HAMMER INTO THE SAFETY (HALF-COCK) POSITION
steps.warn: Finger off the trigger before the hammer moves. Never force it out of half-cock.

steps.title: Read the barrel: .22 Short/Long/Long Rifle or .22 WMR — never mixed
steps.action: Find the caliber marking on the left side of the barrel, toward the receiver, before any ammunition goes back in after cleaning. A rifle marked .22 S-L-L.R. or .22 L-L.R. takes the rimfire Long Rifle family and is not designed for magnums; a rifle marked .22 WMR takes .22 WMR only. The two rifles look almost identical, which is exactly why the barrel marking, not memory, decides. On an L-L.R. rifle Shorts are not recommended.
steps.prose: Winchester says every rimfire version functions best with .22 Long Rifle.
steps.caution: The barrel marking decides the ammunition, not the box you happen to have.
steps.quote: This version of the Model 9422 rifle is not designed to handle 22WMR (magnum) cartridges. All variations of this model are designed to function best with 22 Long Rifle cartridges. .22 L-L.R. Same as above but use of Shorts is not recommended. .22 WMR. This model is made to handle .22 caliber WMR (magnum) calibers only.
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Ammunition

steps.title: Takedown screw out — left side of the receiver
steps.action: With the rifle unloaded, unscrew the takedown screw on the left side of the receiver and remove it completely. Once it is out it is a loose part, so set it somewhere it cannot roll away: it is one of the seven pieces you will put back. Use a screwdriver that fills the slot, because a burred takedown screw is the one visible scar a 9422 collects from being cleaned.
steps.prose: Winchester opens its takedown with the same check you have just done — action open, chamber and magazine tube looked at.
steps.quote: Unscrew and remove takedown screw on left side of receiver (see Figure 4).
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Full Disassembly / Takedown — DISASSEMBLY, step 1

steps.title: Pull the buttstock half down and to the rear
steps.action: Hold the barrel half and pull the buttstock downward and to the rear; the rifle separates into two halves. The buttstock half carries the frame and the finger lever; the barrel half keeps the receiver top, with the barrel fixed to it. It should come away without prying. If it resists, check the takedown screw is fully out rather than levering on the wood.
steps.prose: The barrel is fixed rigidly to the top of the receiver, so a scope mounted on the receiver stays sighted in through a takedown.
steps.caution: Each half carries the serial number; keep the two halves of one rifle together.
steps.quote: Separate the gun into two halves by pulling the butt stock downward to the rear (see Figure 5).
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Full Disassembly / Takedown — DISASSEMBLY, step 2

steps.title: Slide the bolt slide out the back — mind the cam pin
steps.action: Slide the bolt slide rearward out of the receiver, bringing the breech bolt with it. Go slowly and keep the assembly level: the cam pin that joins the bolt to the slide is loose and can drop out as it clears the receiver. A dropped cam pin is small, easy to lose in a carpet, and the rifle will not go back together without it.
steps.prose: Do this over a bench or a towel, not over the floor.
steps.quote: The bolt slide may now be removed by sliding rearward out of receiver (see Figure 6). Use care to prevent the cam pin from dropping free of the bolt.
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Full Disassembly / Takedown — DISASSEMBLY, step 3
steps.warn: The cam pin falls free. Catch it.

steps.title: Separate the breech bolt from the bolt slide
steps.action: Separate the breech bolt from the bolt slide, and put the cam pin with them. That opens the bolt face, the extractor and the ejector to a brush, which is the whole point of taking them out. Do not try to take the extractor or anything else off the bolt: the book stops at bolt and slide apart.
steps.prose: Most of a rimfire's fouling lives on the bolt face and around the extractor, which is why Winchester's cleaning names them.
steps.quote: Bolt and bolt slide may now be separated (see Figure 7).
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Full Disassembly / Takedown — DISASSEMBLY, step 4

steps.title: No further — the rest is a repair centre's job
steps.action: Stop here. Winchester forbids taking the Model 9422 apart any further than this takedown, calls it a finely fitted mechanism, and says you may permanently mar it by trying to disassemble the inner assemblies. Everything still inside the two halves stays where it is. If the rifle needs more than this, the book sends it to an authorized repair centre or a competent gunsmith.
steps.prose: After long periods of heavy use, the book also recommends a qualified gunsmith strip the action for professional cleaning and lubrication.
steps.quote: NEVER ATTEMPT TO TAKE YOUR MODEL 9422 APART FURTHER THAN EXPLAINED IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions — closing NOTICE

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Lay the pieces out and count them: the barrel and forearm half, the buttstock half, the breech bolt, the bolt slide, the cam pin, the magazine tube and the takedown screw. That is the complete takedown Winchester publishes. The bore is now open from the receiver end, and the bolt face, extractor and ejector are free to brush. The cleaning checklist covers each of them.
steps.prose: Seven pieces out means seven pieces back. The cam pin and the takedown screw are the two that go missing.
steps.quote: Your Model 9422 will now be in these pieces: (see Figure 8):
steps.cite: Model 9422 Lever Action Rifle Owner's Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Full Disassembly / Takedown

deepAbsentReason: Winchester's Model 9422 book stops at its takedown: the takedown screw out, the rifle in two halves, and the bolt slide and breech bolt out of the receiver, leaving seven pieces (Full Disassembly / Takedown). It forbids taking the rifle apart further than that and sends further disassembly for service or cleaning to an authorized repair centre or a competent gunsmith (Cleaning and Maintenance Suggestions, closing notice). Its cleaning procedures are done on those seven pieces and are in the cleaning checklist. There is no deeper procedure in the book to walk.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Take the rifle down into its two halves first — Winchester does this to protect the rifling at the muzzle
Rod, tip and snug-fitting patch for the .22 bore, entered at the RECEIVER end and run back and forth
Solvent-saturated patch for a normal amount of powder residue
Brass bore brush with solvent only for heavy fouling, pushed completely through before it is withdrawn
Wipe the bore dry, then pass one slightly oiled patch with a fine, light gun oil
Cleaning it assembled instead? Action open and ejection port turned DOWN so cleaner does not run into the action
⚠ Look into the barrel and chamber for a patch left behind, and remove it

cleaning.name: BOLT, BOLT SLIDE & RECEIVER
tasks: Solvent and a toothbrush around the extractor, ejector and the other small breech bolt parts
Breech bolt and bolt slide especially clean, then lightly oiled with a high-quality gun oil
Remove any dried oil from the receiver area
Thin film of oil on the polished receiver and action surfaces
Keep the cam pin with the bolt — it is loose once bolt and slide are apart
Never pour oil into the receiver — it drains into the wood, softens it and loosens the stock

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Wipe the exposed metal of receiver, forearm and barrel with a clean rag and remove finger marks
Light film of oil on the metal any time the rifle has seen weather or handling
Wipe all wood with a soft cloth — laminated stocks get the same care as walnut
Check the rear sight blade screws and the front sight base screw are tight
Case it for transport; store it dry, out of reach of children, ammunition stored separately
After long, heavy use the action goes to a qualified gunsmith for professional cleaning

reassembly: Assemble the breech bolt and bolt slide, keeping the cam pin centred.
Insert the bolt assembly into the receiver from the rear and push it forward until it locks.
Pull the hammer back to full cock and close the finger lever.
Slide the frame (the buttstock half) into the receiver from the rear.
Insert and tighten the takedown screw on the left side of the receiver.
Lower the hammer from full cock to the half-cock safety position: thumb holding the spur, just enough trigger to release it, finger off, then ease it down.
If the inner magazine tube is out, push it home and lock it — it is under spring tension, so keep control of it.
fncheck: With the rifle unloaded and no ammunition on the bench, look through the bore from the receiver end and confirm no patch is left in the barrel or chamber. Work the finger lever fully down and up several times: it should run smoothly and close fully, and the hammer should come back to full cock. Lower the hammer to half-cock under your thumb and confirm it catches and holds there — do not force the trigger to test it, because Winchester warns that strains the parts and weakens the safety. Confirm the takedown screw is tight, and if a hammer extension is fitted, check it is still tight, since the book warns they loosen with use. Leave the hammer at half-cock. Winchester says never to test the rifle's function with live ammunition.
